summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, Marburg, and the Manjushree Centre of Tibetan Culture. She served as Käthe-Leichter-Gastprofessorin at Vienna (~2004–2005) and Privatdozentin at Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate and habilitation at Hamburg, studying under Ludwig Alsdorf. She held professorships at the University of Münster (1971; 1988–2000) and the University of Munich (1978; 1980).

Aden Kumler is a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, Harvard University, and the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies. She served as Assistant Professor at Chicago (2007–2020) and became Professor at Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche, and later taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He founded The Proletarian and La Typographie française, co-founded the Société Ethnologique de Paris, where he served as vice-president, and served as Résident de France at Kratie, Cambodia.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indology scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Mumbai and studied at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He held posts at Rajaram College (1930–1962), Shivaji University (1962–1971), and the University of Mysore (1971).

Adolf Attenhofer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Zurich, Geneva, Paris, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He served as a teacher at Bündner Kantonsschule (~1908–1944) and founded and directed the Bündner Volkshochschule (1924).
Adolf Erhart was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Masaryk University's Faculty of Arts (~1945–1949) under Václav Machek. He later served as Professor at Masaryk University from 1988 to 1993.

Adolf Erman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Französisches Gymnasium Berlin, Leipzig under Georg Ebers, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the Egyptian Museum of Berlin (~1883–1923).
Adolf Faust was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Strasbourg by 1877 and worked as a school-teacher (Professor) at Gymnasium Mulhouse.

Adolf Friedrich was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at Frankfurt under Leo Frobenius and Hermann Lommel. He held Privatdozent posts at Vienna (1942) and Mainz (1946), later working at Frankfurt (~1947–1950).
Adolf Friedrich Hermann Paul Gärtchen was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Breslau (1900–1905), where he studied under Otto Hoffmann and Alfred Hillebrandt.

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Bonn, Paris, and Berlin, completing his PhD under Franz Bopp. He served as Professor (1833–1847) and Rektor (1862–1863) at the University of Breslau.

Adolf Friedrich von Schack was an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who completed law studies between 1833 and 1838 at the University of Bonn, Heidelberg University, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Adolf Holtzmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin under Schleiermacher, Munich under Frank and Schmeller, and Paris under Burnouf. He was Professor at Bismarck-Gymnasium Karlsruhe (1837) and Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

Adolf Holtzmann Jr. was an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg under Adolf Holtzmann, Erlangen-Nuremberg under Friedrich von Spiegel, and under Rudolf von Roth. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the University of Freiburg from 1885 to 1914.

Adolf Janáček was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Charles University (~1921–1926). He also studied at its Faculty of Arts, First Faculty of Medicine, and the Examination Board for Teachers at Secondary Schools.

Adolf Kaegi was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Zurich, Leipzig, and Tübingen, working under Rudolf von Roth and others. He taught at Kantonsschule Rämibühl (1875–1893) and held professorships at the University of Zurich from 1875 to 1914.

Adolf Kiessling studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1856–1858). He held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1877), the University of Greifswald (~1877–1889), and the University of Göttingen (~1889–1893).

Adolf Kirchhoff was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He taught at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium, joined the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and was professor at Berlin from 1865 to 1908.
